The two spells create two Clues and make Bearer a 6/5 with double strike and trample; sacrificing those Clues makes Ravenous Intruder 5/6. Bearer necessarily deals combat damage during the first-strike step because the three damaged Plants can absorb at most one damage each, creating a third Clue that can be sacrificed to make the Intruder 7/8 before normal combat damage. 1. Tap your 5 Mountains and 2 Spirebluff Canals to add 7 mana to your mana pool.
2. Cast **Savage Alliance** for its Escalate cost by paying {3}{R}. Choose the first and third modes: target yourself so your creatures gain trample, and target your opponent to deal 1 damage to each of their creatures.
3. This triggers both **Trail of Evidence** (creating a Clue token) and **Bearer of Overwhelming Truths**'s Prowess (giving it +1/+1). 
4. Allow Savage Alliance to resolve. Your creatures gain trample until end of turn. Each of the opponent's three 1/2 Plant tokens takes 1 damage (meaning they now effectively have 1 toughness remaining to be assigned lethal damage).
5. Cast **Uncaged Fury** for {2}{R}, targeting **Bearer of Overwhelming Truths**.
6. This again triggers Trail of Evidence (creating a second Clue token) and Prowess (giving Bearer another +1/+1).
7. Allow Uncaged Fury to resolve. Bearer of Overwhelming Truths gets +1/+1 and Double Strike. It is now a 6/5 creature with Double Strike and Trample.
8. Activate **Ravenous Intruder**'s ability twice, sacrificing the two Clue tokens. It gets +4/+4, becoming a 5/6 creature with Trample.
9. Move to the Combat Phase and declare both Bearer of Overwhelming Truths and Ravenous Intruder as attackers.
10. The opponent declares blockers with their three 1/2 Plants (which only require 1 damage each to be destroyed). No matter how they block, they can at most absorb 3 total damage across all assigned blockers.
11. Move to the **First Strike Combat Damage Step**. Bearer of Overwhelming Truths assigns 6 damage. It assigns 1 lethal damage to each Plant blocking it, and the remainder tramples over to the opponent. Because there are at most 3 Plants, Bearer will deal at least 3 damage to the opponent. 
12. Because Bearer of Overwhelming Truths successfully dealt combat damage to a player, its triggered ability goes on the stack. Allow it to resolve to investigate, creating a third Clue token.
13. Before leaving the First Strike damage step (when players get priority), activate Ravenous Intruder's ability, sacrificing the newly created Clue token. Ravenous Intruder gets +2/+2, becoming a 7/8 creature with Trample.
14. Move to the **Normal Combat Damage Step**. Bearer of Overwhelming Truths assigns its normal combat damage. All blockers assigned to it were already destroyed, so it deals a full 6 damage to the opponent. Ravenous Intruder (now a 7/8) assigns 1 lethal damage to any surviving Plants blocking it, and the rest tramples over to the opponent.
15. In total, your attacking creatures have a combined effective power of 19 across both damage steps (6 First Strike + 6 Normal + 7 Normal). The opponent's three Plants will absorb exactly 3 of that damage before dying. The remaining 16 damage tramples over to the opponent, reducing their life total from 16 to exactly 0. You win!

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.
